questions.prompt: Which people built Stonehenge's largest stones into place?
questions.fact: The smaller bluestones were brought roughly 250 kilometres from Wales, which remains hard to explain.

questions.prompt: What is the term for the rate of change of velocity?
questions.fact: Turning at constant speed still counts, since direction is part of velocity.

questions.prompt: In tennis, what surface is the Australian Open played on?
questions.fact: It was played on grass until 1988, when it moved venues and changed surface at the same time.

questions.prompt: Which musician released the album Random Access Memories?
questions.fact: It was recorded largely with live session musicians, deliberately avoiding the sampling the duo was known for.

questions.prompt: Which US state borders the Pacific and Canada?
questions.fact: Its Olympic Peninsula contains one of the few temperate rainforests in the northern hemisphere.

questions.prompt: Who wrote the novel Rebecca's Cornish-set predecessor, Jamaica Inn?
questions.fact: The inn is a real building, and she stayed there after getting lost on the moor in fog.

questions.prompt: What is the term for a fixed-size numeric identifier produced from data?
questions.fact: Two different inputs producing the same one is called a collision, and finding them deliberately breaks a hash function.
